label: Farming and agribusiness
tagline: Plan a harvest across your fields
opening: You've started as the farm planner at **<<biz>>**. Planting is done and harvest is coming. The farm manager wants a program that forecasts every field before the crews are booked.
rule: Harvest crews are expensive. A crew is only sent to fields of **more than <<level>> hectares**. Smaller fields are cut by hand.
scene: The manager calls from the road: "How big is the <<n2>>?" You shouldn't have to find the paper map. The planner needs a quick lookup, and it must cope with fields you don't farm.

action.name: needs_crew
action.doc: say whether the field is big enough for a harvest crew

glossary: 10,000 square metres of land, a little over one football pitch.
How much a crop produces per hectare, usually in tonnes.
An estimate of the crop before it is cut: hectares times yield.
The weeks when seed must go in the ground to ripen on time.
A specialist who advises on crops and soil.
A farmer working a small plot, often by hand.
Crop spoiled after cutting through poor storage or transport.
py_uses: Forecast yields from weather and soil data
Schedule harvest crews by field size
Warn about frost before it damages crops
